trigger: first fleet catalogue page with N connected agents (runs whenever the rollup meta is non-null, even while building); material from N ~ 10^5
classification_rationale: NEW-EVIDENCE against accepted debt (b): cov.connected = device_api->list_devices().size() calls AgentRegistry::to_json_obj(), which builds a JSON object per agent while holding the registry mutex mu_ (agent_registry.cpp:839-840), the same mutex touch_activity/send_to/get_session take; AgentRegistry::agent_count() is O(1). The same pattern pre-exists on GET /api/v1/devices, so this adds a caller, not a new class; the bounded per-call stall keeps it MEDIUM (no raise: not a wedge, not unbounded)
summary: The coverage.connected gather delays heartbeat and dispatch bookkeeping for ~1-2 microseconds per connected agent per first-page load (about 10 ms at 6,000, seconds at 2M). Needs a DeviceApi count accessor (a new in-process public contract: Test 1 -> split/file). Draft issue 01.

trigger: a broad q (or the per-page totals scan) that exceeds the 5 s statement bound at fleet scale: it fails identically on every retry
classification_rationale: bounded_query maps pool timeout, query error and the 5 s statement timeout to one nullopt (software_inventory_store.cpp:473-509) and sw_fail_degraded sends retry_after_ms 5000 for all of them; a deterministic timeout invites a retry loop that holds a PG backend 5 s per attempt and bumps the degrade counter (alert YuzuInventoryReadDegraded); unreachable below the PR-1 refresh ceiling (~6,000 endpoints, #5545)
summary: A deterministic statement timeout is reported as a retryable 503 with a fixed 5000 ms hint (unhappy-path UP-3, sre F4, performance F3). Needs a store-level reason (new internal contract: Test 1 -> split/file). Draft issue 03.

trigger: a saturated PG pool or slow database: a first page makes up to 4 sequential leases (3 s acquire, 5 s statement each) plus count_stale_agents, doubled on a generation move; an export up to 14 leases
classification_rationale: no end-to-end deadline: worst case ~22-44 s per page and ~50-60 s per export pinning one httplib worker; a client timeout does not cancel the handler so its retry stacks on the abandoned request; leases are sequential and the pool fast-fails, so not a wedge (I5 base MEDIUM, no raise); the pattern is shared with other PG-backed read handlers
summary: No total time budget for a catalogue request (unhappy-path UP-4). A reusable request budget is a new bounded-wait mechanism (Test 1 -> split/file). Draft issue 04.
